business_problem: Wella needed to respond to changing beauty-market dynamics and declining traditional salon profitability as professionals shifted to freelance models. Its existing approach did not provide the cohesive digital ecosystem needed to improve customer outreach, serve salons and independent stylists effectively, and meet demand for personalized digital-first buying experiences.
solution_summary: Infosys helped Wella rework its B2B commerce operation through a three-phase transformation - Initiate, Enhance, and Accelerate - that shifted the company from a traditional sales model to a digital-first architecture. The implementation moved Wella's e-commerce platforms to a headless architecture so storefront experiences, mobile channels, and partner touchpoints could evolve more flexibly. Within that commerce layer, Infosys integrated advanced AI features to generate tailored product recommendations for salon owners and independent stylists, using shopping-context signals from the digital experience to improve relevance and cross-sell potential. The program also connected external eRetailers, payment-processing partners, education platforms, personalized promotions, and operational tools into one omnichannel ecosystem. While the source does not identify a storage tier, it clearly describes an integrated serving and orchestration stack for B2B ordering and engagement.
